paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: Suppose the university newspaper is inviting submissions from the students for its coming edition on what in their university impresses them most. You are now to write an essay for submission. You will have 30 minutes to write the essay. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：假设大学报纸正在邀请学生为其即将出版的报纸投稿，内容是他们大学中最让他们印象深刻的事情。您现在需要写一篇论文以供提交。你将有 30 分钟的时间来写这篇文章。您应该写至少 120 个字但不超过 180 个字。

paragraphs.sourceText: Exercising for just 10 minutes a week is linked to a longer life, according to a new study published in The British Journal of Sports Medicine.
paragraphs.translationZh: 《英国运动医学杂志》发表的一项新研究表明，每周锻炼 10 分钟就可以延长寿命。

paragraphs.sourceText: Several recent studies have found that even low-intensity exercise, done for a short amount of time, can have a meaningful 26 on health. Still, the idea that exercising for just 10 minutes a week may be enough to increase your lifespan is novel. It’s also somewhat 27 , since the federal physical activity guidelines recommend getting at least 75 minutes of vigorous exercise or 150 minutes of 28 exercise each week.
paragraphs.translationZh: 最近的几项研究发现，即使是短时间的低强度运动，也可以对健康产生有意义的影响。尽管如此，每周锻炼 10 分钟就足以延长寿命的想法还是很新颖的。这也存在一些争议，因为联邦体育活动指南建议每周至少进行 75 分钟的剧烈运动或 150 分钟的适度运动。

paragraphs.sourceText: The study was based on data from more than 88,000 U.S. adults who 29 in the National Health Interview Survey between 1997 and 2008.
paragraphs.translationZh: 该研究基于 1997 年至 2008 年间参加全国健康访谈调查的 88,000 多名美国成年人的数据。

paragraphs.sourceText: Contrary to some research that has found an 30 limit to the amount of exercise that is healthy, the researchers found that there was 31 no limit to the longevity (长寿) benefits of exercise. Even the small group of people who got 10 times the amount of exercise recommended by the federal government had a 46% lower 32 of death than the least active group.
paragraphs.translationZh: 与一些研究发现健康运动量有上限相反，研究人员发现运动对长寿的好处似乎没有限制。即使是运动量达到联邦政府建议 10 倍的一小群人，其死亡风险也比运动量最少的群体低 46%。

paragraphs.sourceText: Still, observational studies like this one cannot prove cause and effect; they can only find 33 . The researchers also were not able to 34 for certain lifestyle factors that could affect lifespan, including dietary habits and changes in physical activity over time. Despite these 35 , the study’s results are yet another indication of the power of physical activity, even in small amounts.
paragraphs.translationZh: 尽管如此，像这样的观察性研究并不能证明因果关系。他们只能找到模式。研究人员也无法调整某些可能影响寿命的生活方式因素，包括饮食习惯和身体活动随时间的变化。尽管存在这些局限性，该研究的结果再次表明了体力活动的力量，即使是少量的体力活动。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: How Climate Change Will Affect What You Eat
paragraphs.translationZh: 气候变化将如何影响你的饮食

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Earlier this year, scientists warned that one in six animal species could go extinct (灭绝的) due to climate change. Could the same thing happen to our crops and other foodstuffs too?
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 今年早些时候，科学家警告说，六分之一的动物物种可能因气候变化而灭绝。同样的事情也会发生在我们的农作物和其他食品上吗？

paragraphs.sourceText: B) It’s clear that farmers in many parts of the world are going to find things harder in the coming decades. Last week, BBC Future explored one scientist’s efforts to help crops cope with the increased probability of droughts. By using the genes from resurrection (复活) plants, Jill Farrant of the University of Cape Town is exploring whether she can design crops to survive for much longer periods without water.
paragraphs.translationZh: B）很明显，世界许多地区的农民在未来几十年里会发现事情变得更加困难。上周，BBC Future 探讨了一位科学家为帮助作物应对日益增加的干旱可能性所做的努力。开普敦大学的吉尔·法兰特 (Jill Farrant) 正在利用复活植物的基因，探索是否可以设计出能够在没有水的情况下存活更长时间的作物。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) But if we can’t find ways to protect other foods, will they survive climate change? Fortunately, there is some good news on this front. Despite alarmist headlines about “foods that are going extinct,” there is no evidence that major food types like beans, chocolate, wine, corn or wheat will cease to exist.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 但如果我们找不到保护其他食物的方法，它们能在气候变化中生存下来吗？幸运的是，这方面有一些好消息。尽管有关于“食物即将灭绝”的危言耸听的头条新闻，但没有证据表明豆类、巧克力、葡萄酒、玉米或小麦等主要食物类型将不复存在。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) But that doesn’t mean it’s all good news for future food. We will probably have to change where we grow certain crops, as some regions get too hot. The disadvantage, obviously, is that local farmers will suffer under this situation. And some people may struggle to get the same access to certain foods. “Even if overall food production may be unaffected, food security can still be impacted,” says Margaret Walsh, a scientist at the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Climate Change Program Office. In other words, even if a certain food is still grown on some corner of the Earth, it doesn’t mean that everyone will continue to have the same degree of access as today.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 但这并不意味着这对未来的食品来说都是好消息。由于某些地区变得太热，我们可能不得不改变某些作物的种植地点。显然，缺点是当地农民将在这种情况下遭受损失。有些人可能很难以同样的方式获得某些食物。美国农业部气候变化项目办公室科学家玛格丽特·沃尔什表示：“即使总体粮食生产可能不受影响，粮食安全仍可能受到影响。”换句话说，即使某种食物仍然生长在地球的某个角落，并不意味着每个人都将继续拥有与今天相同程度的获取机会。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) Overall, the yields of many foods, from staples to life-enhancing extras such as coffee and chocolate, will likely be impacted by climate change too. How those decreases will be felt will depend on the degree of warming and the crop in question, but in general, “anything over about 30°C is very bad for crops,” says Wolfram Schlenker, an associate professor of international and public affairs at Columbia University. For example, statistical studies that he and a colleague built of corn and soybean (大豆) production in the U.S. show a steep decline after crossing the 30°C temperature threshold (临界点).
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 总体而言，许多食物的产量，从主食到咖啡和巧克力等改善生活的额外食品，也可能会受到气候变化的影响。哥伦比亚大学国际与公共事务副教授沃尔弗拉姆·施伦克 (Wolfram Schlenker) 表示，如何感受到这些下降取决于变暖的程度和所涉及的作物，但总的来说，“任何超过 30°C 的温度都对作物非常不利”。例如，他和一位同事对美国玉米和大豆（大豆）产量进行的统计研究表明，在超过 30°C 温度阈值（临界点）后，产量急剧下降。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) In the U.S. — the world’s largest producer of corn and soybeans — farms can move north to some degree, Schlenker says. But eventually, yields will likely suffer because the soil north of Iowa declines in quality — a legacy of glacial (冰川的) expansion. Other studies, including studies of wheat in India and corn in Africa, also found that there is a threshold above which yields sharply decline: crops can adapt and move, but only to a point. “What’s common to all studies is the finding that extreme heat is damaging to crop growth, although exact cutoffs vary by crop,” Schlenker says. “If predictions for the end of the century are true, though, I think a lot of agricultural areas in the U.S. will see significant hits.”
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 施伦克说，在美国——世界上最大的玉米和大豆生产国——农场可以在某种程度上向北迁移。但最终，产量可能会受到影响，因为爱荷华州北部的土壤质量下降——这是冰川扩张的产物。其他研究，包括对印度小麦和非洲玉米的研究，也发现存在一个阈值，超过该阈值产量就会急剧下降：农作物可以适应和移动，但只能在一定程度上。 “所有研究的共同点是发现极端高温会损害作物生长，尽管具体的截止值因作物而异，”施伦克说。 “不过，如果本世纪末的预测属实，我认为美国的许多农业地区将遭受重大打击。”

paragraphs.sourceText: G) Under current conditions, about 4% of the world’s croplands experience drought in any given year, but by the end of the century those conditions are forecasted to jump to about 18% per year. Some studies indicate that horticulture crops — generally, everything besides staples — may be impacted most severely, largely because they tend to be confined to a smaller geographic area. Researcher Andrew Jarvis and his colleagues found that 80% of coffee-growing zones in Central America and Brazil could become unsuitable by 2050, for example, while climate change will likely have “great impacts” on cocoa (可可粉) production in West Africa. “High quality chocolate will be less available in the future, and if you want it, you’ll have to pay a lot more for it,” Jarvis says.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 在目前的情况下，世界上约 4% 的农田在任何一年都会经历干旱，但到本世纪末，预计这种情况将跃升至每年 18% 左右。一些研究表明，园艺作物——一般来说，除了主食之外的所有作物——可能受到最严重的影响，很大程度上是因为它们往往局限于较小的地理区域。例如，研究员安德鲁·贾维斯 (Andrew Jarvis) 和他的同事发现，到 2050 年，中美洲和巴西 80% 的咖啡种植区可能变得不适宜种植，而气候变化可能会对西非的可可粉生产产生“巨大影响”。贾维斯说：“未来高质量的巧克力将会越来越少，如果你想要它，你将不得不付出更多的钱。”

paragraphs.sourceText: H) This means that, for those who can afford it, some foods will simply cost them more in the future. But for poorer people, those same price jumps will likely cause certain foods to go extinct from their diets. “The more you reduce, the shorter the supply, and the higher the price will jump,” Schlenker says.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 这意味着，对于那些负担得起的人来说，某些食物将来只会花费更多。但对于较贫穷的人来说，同样的价格上涨可能会导致某些食物从他们的饮食中消失。 “减少的越多，供应就越短，价格就会跳得越高，”施伦克说。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Another potential climate change-induced problem is our dependence on commodity crops — wheat, soybeans, corn and rice — which currently provide humanity with 75% of its calories, either directly or indirectly through the animals we raise on those crops. Jarvis and his colleagues also found that, over the past five decades, the world has seen an increasing standardisation of diets; the foods we eat globally today are 36% more similar than they were in 1961. While this can be good news for the world’s poorest people who now consume more calories, protein and fat than in the past, homogeneity (同一性) and over-dependence on a handful of staples leaves us vulnerable to threats such as drought, disease and pests — all of which are predicted to worsen in many parts of the world as a result of climate change.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 气候变化引起的另一个潜在问题是我们对商品作物（小麦、大豆、玉米和大米）的依赖，目前这些作物为人类提供了 75% 的卡路里，直接或间接通过我们在这些作物上饲养的动物提供。贾维斯和他的同事还发现，在过去的五年里，世界饮食的标准化程度不断提高。我们今天在全球范围内吃的食物比 1961 年相似了 36%。虽然这对于世界上最贫穷的人们来说可能是个好消息，他们现在比过去消耗更多的卡路里、蛋白质和脂肪，但同质性和对少数主食的过度依赖使我们容易受到干旱、疾病和虫害等威胁的影响——预计由于气候变化，所有这些威胁都会在世界许多地区恶化。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) There are ways we could soften the coming blow to the global food supply, however. Like Farrant’s work with resurrection crops, a number of companies, organisations and researchers are aiming to create drought- and temperature-resistant crops through genetic engineering and conventional breeding. For now, the jury is still out as to how successful those endeavours will be. “The people at Monsanto who I’ve talked to are much more optimistic that they’ll be able to engineer heat-tolerant crops,” Schlenker says. “On the other hand, scientists at the USDA who I’ve spoken with are much more cautious.”
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 然而，我们有一些方法可以减轻全球粮食供应即将受到的打击。与法兰特在复活作物方面的研究一样，许多公司、组织和研究人员都致力于通过基因工程和传统育种来培育耐旱和耐温的作物。目前，这些努力能否成功尚无定论。 “与我交谈过的孟山都公司的人对他们能够培育耐热作物更加乐观，”施伦克说。 “另一方面，与我交谈过的美国农业部的科学家则要谨慎得多。”

paragraphs.sourceText: K) Until genetic engineering comes to fruition, other strategies might also help in some places, including applying more fertiliser, implementing better irrigation, using machinery that gets crops out of the field faster or installing storage facilities to delay spoilage. “Many places could benefit a great deal just by using technologies that already exist,” Walsh says. “General farm management can go a long way toward easing changes.”
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 在基因工程取得成果之前，其他策略也可能在某些地方有所帮助，包括施用更多肥料、实施更好的灌溉、使用更快地将农作物运出田地的机械或安装储存设施以延缓腐败。沃尔什说：“许多地方只要使用现有的技术就可以受益匪浅。” “一般农场管理对于缓解变化大有帮助。”

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Finally, diversifying our diet away from heat-sensitive wheat, corn, rice and other crops could also help. “We’ve seen profound changes in the last decades in what we eat largely as a result of international trade, and I think that trend toward more diversification will continue,” Jarvis says. “Depending on a greater number of plant species creates a more vigorous and less risky food system — and one that provides a broader range of nutritional requirements.”
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 最后，使我们的饮食多样化，远离对热敏感的小麦、玉米、大米和其他作物也可能有所帮助。贾维斯说：“过去几十年来，我们的饮食发生了深刻的变化，这主要是由于国际贸易的结果，我认为更加多样化的趋势将继续下去。” “依赖更多的植物物种创造了一个更有活力、风险更低的食物系统，并且可以提供更广泛的营养需求。”

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. One consequence of climate change is that some people may not have adequate access to certain foods.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 气候变化的后果之一是一些人可能无法充分获得某些食物。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. People around the world are eating foods more similar than what they used to eat.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 世界各地的人们吃的食物比以前吃的更加相似。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. A recent news report talked about scientific efforts to help crops survive droughts through genetic engineering.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 最近的一篇新闻报道谈到了通过基因工程帮助农作物抵御干旱的科学努力。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. It is predicted that climate change will affect the availability and price of quality chocolate.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 据预测，气候变化将影响优质巧克力的供应和价格。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. People wonder if certain crops and foodstuffs could disappear like some animal species due to climate change.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 人们想知道某些农作物和食品是否会像某些动物物种一样因气候变化而消失。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Although farms in the U.S. can move a bit northward, crop yields may decrease.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 虽然美国的农场可以向北移动一点，但农作物产量可能会下降。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. One possible solution to the food security problem is diversification of diet.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 粮食安全问题的一种可能解决办法是饮食多样化。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. It remains unsettled whether the global food supply problem can be solved by creating heat-tolerant crops through genetic engineering.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 全球粮食供应问题是否可以通过基因工程培育耐热作物来解决，这一问题仍悬而未决。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. Poor people may have to give up eating certain foods because of their high prices.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 穷人可能因为某些食物价格高昂而不得不放弃食用。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. A number of existing farming technologies could be used to reduce the negative effect of climate change on food production.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 一些现有的农业技术可用于减少气候变化对粮食生产的负面影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：本节有 2 段。每段文章后面都有一些问题或未完成的陈述。每个选项都有四个选项，标记为 A)、B)、C) 和 D)。您应该决定最佳选择，并在答题卡 2 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: One of my bad habits is saying “busy” when people ask me how I’m doing. Sometimes it’s because I actually am busy, but other times it’s because that’s what I think I’m supposed to say. That’s what important people say. That’s what people who get promoted say. But working long hours doesn’t drive better results. Never taking a vacation won’t lead to a promotion. So why are we so proud to talk about how busy we are all the time?
paragraphs.translationZh: 我的坏习惯之一是当人们问我过得怎么样时说“忙”。有时是因为我实际上很忙，但有时是因为我认为我应该说这些。这就是重要人物所说的。升职的人都是这么说的。但长时间工作并不会带来更好的结果。不休假不会带来晋升。那么，为什么我们如此自豪地谈论我们一直有多忙呢？

paragraphs.sourceText: In 2016, researchers from Columbia, Harvard, and Georgetown conducted a study to figure it out. They found busy people are perceived to be of high status, and interestingly, these status attributions are heavily influenced by our own beliefs about social mobility. In other words, the more we believe that one has the opportunity for success based on hard work, the more we tend to think that people who skip leisure and work all the time are of higher standing.
paragraphs.translationZh: 2016年，哥伦比亚大学、哈佛大学和乔治城大学的研究人员进行了一项研究来找出答案。他们发现忙碌的人被认为具有很高的地位，有趣的是，这些地位归因很大程度上受到我们自己对社会流动性的信念的影响。换句话说，我们越相信一个人通过努力工作就能获得成功，我们就越倾向于认为那些总是不休息、不工作的人地位更高。

paragraphs.sourceText: That’s why we feel like we have to appear busy, and there’s a real perception that if someone is knee-deep in meetings, emails and stress, then they’re probably a big deal. This culture of busyness is making it hard for employees to find work-life balance. According to a recent study, one in five highly engaged employees are at risk of burnout (精疲力竭).
paragraphs.translationZh: 这就是为什么我们觉得自己必须表现得很忙碌，而且有一种真实的感觉，如果有人忙于会议、电子邮件和压力，那么他们可能是个大问题。这种忙碌的文化使员工很难找到工作与生活的平衡。根据最近的一项研究，五分之一高度敬业的员工面临精疲力尽的风险。

paragraphs.sourceText: Personally, I’m going to stop saying “busy” when people ask me how I am. It sounds self-righteous (自以为是的) and sets the wrong tone. Phrases like “I have limited access to email” and “I’ll respond as soon as I get back” sound like you’re being held against your will from working as opposed to making the most of your time off.
paragraphs.translationZh: 就我个人而言，当人们问我过得怎么样时，我将不再说“忙”。这听起来很自以为是，而且定下了错误的基调。像“我对电子邮件的访问权限有限”和“我一回来就会回复”这样的短语听起来就像你被迫无法工作，而不是充分利用你的休息时间。

paragraphs.sourceText: That’s why we recently launched the Out of Office Email Generator, a free tool you can use before your next long weekend or trip. You can share loud and proud that you won’t be checking email until you’re back. Managers need to think twice about emailing their teams on the weekend and talking about how busy they are. Leaders should take time off themselves and encourage employees to do the same.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这就是为什么我们最近推出了外出电子邮件生成器，这是一个免费工具，您可以在下一个长周末或旅行之前使用。您可以自豪地大声分享，在回来之前您不会查看电子邮件。经理们需要三思而后行，不要在周末给团队发电子邮件并谈论他们有多忙。领导者应该给自己放假，并鼓励员工也这样做。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Female employees consistently pay lower airfares than men do for the same flights because they tend to book earlier.
paragraphs.translationZh: 对于相同的航班，女性员工支付的机票价格始终低于男性员工，因为她们往往更早预订。

paragraphs.sourceText: We compared the airfare paid by employees in the same position within a company for the same class of travel and used a common statistical technique to account for other factors that might affect differences in airfares. We found that women paid on average $18 less per ticket than their male colleagues. Further investigation allowed us to conclude that this gap is largely explained by the fact that women tended to book earlier than men, 1.8 days on average.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们比较了公司内相同职位的员工为同一舱位旅行支付的机票价格，并使用通用统计技术来考虑可能影响机票价格差异的其他因素。我们发现，女性每张门票的费用比男性同事平均少 18 美元。进一步的调查让我们得出结论，这种差距很大程度上是由于女性往往比男性更早预订，平均提前 1.8 天。

paragraphs.sourceText: We wanted to determine what was causing these gender differences in booking business trips so we tested a variety of possible explanations, such as women choosing to plan ahead or male frequent travelers being inclined to book late. None of these explained away the gender gap, so we applied data collected from surveys that express consumer preferences that play a central role in economic decisions, such as patience and risk avoidance.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们想要确定导致商务旅行预订方面存在性别差异的原因，因此我们测试了各种可能的解释，例如女性选择提前计划或男性常旅客倾向于延迟预订。这些都无法解释性别差距，因此我们应用了从调查中收集的数据，这些数据表达了在经济决策中发挥核心作用的消费者偏好，例如耐心和风险规避。

paragraphs.sourceText: We found that only the concept of “negative reciprocity” — in which an employee who feels unfairly treated engages in negative behaviors, such as spending their company’s money less carefully — explains these differences. The surveys showed men tend to exhibit more of these negative behaviors than women. This isn’t to say that all men engage in these behaviors — or that booking relatively late is a sign of abnormal behavior. It only means that the gender gap disappears when we plug in the negative reciprocity variable.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们发现，只有“负互惠”的概念——即感觉受到不公平待遇的员工会做出负面行为，比如不小心花公司的钱——才能解释这些差异。调查显示，男性比女性更容易表现出这些负面行为。这并不是说所有男性都会有这些行为，或者说相对较晚的预订是异常行为的表现。这仅意味着当我们插入负互惠变量时，性别差距消失。

paragraphs.sourceText: Prior research on negative reciprocity among workers found that it can result in lower employee motivation, business performance and workplace morale (士气) and culture.
paragraphs.translationZh: 先前对员工之间的负互惠的研究发现，它会导致员工积极性、业务绩效、工作场所士气和文化下降。

paragraphs.sourceText: Our results show another way these negative behaviors can manifest themselves, like in airline bookings, and add to evidence that women are less likely to engage in them.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们的研究结果显示了这些负面行为的另一种表现方式，例如在机票预订中，并进一步证明女性不太可能参与这些行为。

paragraphs.sourceText: Companies spend significant sums of money on business travel. While that $18 difference per ticket may seem small, it adds up. Our analysis suggests early booking by women can translate into savings of $1 million a year for a large multinational company with 20,000 regular travelers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 公司在商务旅行上花费了大量资金。虽然每张票 18 美元的差额看似很小，但加起来就很大了。我们的分析表明，对于一家拥有 20,000 名常客的大型跨国公司来说，女性提前预订每年可以节省 100 万美元。

paragraphs.sourceText: 51. What did the author’s team conclude about the gender difference in airfares from their further investigation?
paragraphs.translationZh: 51. 作者团队通过进一步调查，得出了哪些关于机票价格性别差异的结论？

paragraphs.sourceText: 52. What did the researchers want to determine by testing a variety of possible explanations?
paragraphs.translationZh: 52. 通过测试各种可能的解释，研究人员想确定什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: 53. What happened when the negative reciprocity variable was taken into account?
paragraphs.translationZh: 53.当考虑负互易变量时会发生什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: 54. What did prior research on negative reciprocity among workers find?
paragraphs.translationZh: 54. 先前关于工人之间负互惠的研究发现了什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: 55. What does the author emphasize about their analysis in the last paragraph?
paragraphs.translationZh: 55.作者在最后一段中强调了他们的分析是什么？
